messages:
Emma: FYI support opened an escalation — customer saw mixed 503 + 429 during a long ramp. They ran a DIY client that does 200RPM steady then 2kRPM bursts for 3m and hit throttles. Can we run a coordinated bakeoff to pick sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst windows?

Mike: Which customer / tenant? we should repro in a tenant-sim first, not prod.

Emma: @Mike it was ACME-42 (sandbox). They shared a snippet of their load client, attaching the pattern below. No PII.

Lavanya: Paste the client pattern here? also: were the 429s global rate limits or per-key caps?

Emma: Snippet they used:```bash
# simple spike: steady 200rpm for 20m, then 2k rpm burst for 3m, repeat x3
./loadgen --rpm 200 --duration 1200 
sleep 180
./loadgen --rpm 2000 --duration 180
```
They said 503 during the burst ramp and 429s shortly after.

Jon: Key facts to confirm: 1) Is this multi-key (many users) or single API key? 2) client used exponential backoff?

Emma: Single API key (customer test key), no backoff in the client.

Mike: OK, single-key spike + no backoff explains exhaustion of token-based quota and also backend queue pressure causing 503s. Proposed experiments: a) vary burst window: 30s/60s/180s b) vary token refill (leaky bucket) sizes c) test multi-key vs single-key.

Lavanya: I can run a headless load lab with controlled patterns. Plan: run the following matrix in staging:
- RPM baseline: 100, 200, 500
- Burst RPMs: 1k, 2k, 5k
- Burst windows: 15s, 60s, 180s
- Keys: single-key, 10-key round-robin
Each run 10m, collect 429/503 counts, backend queue depth, p95/p99 latency.

Emma: +1. How do we map results to a recommendation? We want defaults that work for PLG self-serve without developers hitting surprises.

Jon: Heuristic: choose default throttle such that steady RPM = 95th percentile of typical small-app traffic (maybe 200rpm); burst allowance should be lenient but bounded: allow up to 3x steady for <=60s, and require distributed keys for sustained higher throughput.

Mike: For quantifiable policy, we can publish: default per-key steady RPM = 200, short-burst multiplier = 5x for <=30s, medium-burst = 3x for <=60s, long bursts require reserved capacity or dedicated. We need data to confirm those numbers.

Lavanya: Running first matrix now. Using `vegeta` to drive, command:```bash
echo "GET /v1/generate" | vegeta attack -rate=200 -duration=10m | vegeta report
```
I'll push results to the loadbench bucket and post a link.

ops-bot: Deployment notice: staging loadlab support image v1.14 deployed to cluster loadlab-3 at 2026-03-17T15:04:00Z :white_check_mark:

Emma: Good. Also check whether caching/prefix-KV caching kicks in during steady rpm which might mask real query cost. Add a randomized prompt payload so cache hits are low.

Lavanya: Will do randomized seeds. Also will capture model variant fallbacks (e.g., automatic swap to smaller model under load) — record if fallbacks mask errors.

Jon: For alerts/UX: capture which errors users see. If 429s dominate, UI should show quota-exceeded with link to billing/upgrade. If 503s, we need an SRE incident look.

Mike: After matrix, let's run a long run (2h) at medium burst to check stateful effects: kernel thrashing, connection churn, agent memory. Schedule Friday morning 09:00 PT?

Emma: Friday 09:00 PT works. @Lavanya can you call out if any test produces tail latencies >5s or >0.5% 503s? We'll use that as failure criteria.

Lavanya: Noted. I'll post progress and a short summary doc with recommended numeric defaults + rationale after runs.

Mike: If results align, we should update docs: "Default per-key quotas & recommended burst behavior" and add a quick troubleshooting checklist for support (how to distinguish quota vs backend overload).

Emma: Thanks team — please tag me on the summary. :pray:

Jon: tagging follow-ups: #product (for UX messaging) and #support (for playbook updates).

Lavanya: First batch done, uploading charts now (link: https://storage.redwood/lab/results/2076543210-run1). Raw: 429s spiked for single-key 2k bursts >30s, 503s increased when backend queue > 80% capacity.

Emma: Perfect, that's actionable. We'll reconvene post-run to set final numbers. :thumbsup:
